title_ar: الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يحاضر لجمعية المستقبل عن "السلوك الحضاري"ج 2.
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Lectures to the Future Association on "Civilised Conduct", Part 2
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء مساء أمس الأحد في فضاء التنوع الثقافي بالعاصمة انواكشوط محاضرة بعنوان: "السلوك الحضري" [الجزء الثاني]، تحدث الشيخ – حفظه الله – في هذا الجزء من الموضوع عن ضوابط السلوك الحضري في شقيه السياسي والاجتماعي، ففي الجانب السياسي تطرق للأفكار التالية: •- حاجة الناس إلى السياسة وحسن التدبير ممن يسوسهم؛ لأن للناس أملاكا مشتركة لا يمكن أن يستأثر بها أحد دون غيره. •- ما حصل في الأمة الإسلامية من توارث للحكم لم يكن سلوكا حضاريا مقبولا ولا هو من الهدي النبوي الذي أرشد إليه القرآن الكريم. •- السلوك الحضاري المنشود هو ما كان عليه العهد النبوي والخلافة الراشدة. •- الخلافة العثمانية سلكت مسلكا حضاريا مقبولا ثم تراجعت أمام خضم الحضارة الغربية الناشئة. •- ليس لدى الإسلام مانع من استيراد أي فكرة نافعة غير مناقضة لتعاليم الدين الإسلامي الحنيف. •- الديمقراطية إذا طبقت على الوجه الصحيح كانت وسيلة من وسائل تطبيق الشورى، وأدت إلى التداول السلمي للسلطة. •- الحاكم يجب عليه أن يطبق العدل ويسعى للإصلاح، انطلاقا من الآية الكريمة: يَا دَاوُودُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الأَرْضِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ وَلا تَتَّبِعْ الْهَوَى فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا نَسُوا يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ (26) (سورة ص). أما في الجانب الاجتماعي فقد تعرض الشيخ الددو – حفظه الله - لما يتعلق بالعادات في المجتمع الموريتاني، وذكر أن هذه العادات لابد أن توزن بميزان الشرع، ومن ذلك مناسبة الزواج التي يقع فيها الكثير من المسلكيات المنافية للسلوك الحضاري، وما يصاحبها من السرف والتبذير في المال..، ومن ذلك أيضا ما يحسبه الناس في مجتمعنا من الحياء الذي هو في الحقيقة ليس من الحياء في شيء، وهو سلوك بدوي غير مرضي ومناف للسلوك الحضاري أملته ظرفية المجتمع في زمن غابر. ونشير هنا إلى أن المحاضرة تم تنظيمها من قبل جمعية المستقبل التي يرأسها فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو- حفظه الله-، وهي المحاضرة الثانية في هذا الموضوع، وقد حضرها جمع غفير من محبي الشيخ والمهتمين بالشأن الدعوي رجالا ونساءً.
body_en:
His eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture yesterday evening, Sunday, at the Cultural Diversity Space in the capital, Nouakchott, entitled "Urban Conduct" [Part Two]. The Sheikh — may God preserve him — spoke in this part of the subject about the governing criteria of urban conduct in its two aspects, the political and the social. On the political side he dealt with the following ideas:

• People's need for governance and for good management by those who govern them, because people have shared possessions which no one may take exclusively for himself to the exclusion of others.

• That what came about in the Muslim community by way of hereditary succession to rule was not acceptable civilised conduct, nor is it part of the prophetic guidance to which the Noble Qur'an directed.

• The civilised conduct that is sought is what obtained in the prophetic era and the Rightly Guided Caliphate.

• The Ottoman caliphate followed an acceptable civilised course, then fell back before the surge of the rising Western civilisation.

• Islam has no objection to importing any beneficial idea that does not contradict the teachings of the upright Islamic religion.

• Democracy, if applied in the correct manner, was a means among the means of applying consultation (shūrā), and led to the peaceful transfer of power.

• The ruler is obliged to apply justice and to strive for reform, proceeding from the noble verse: {O David, We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between people with truth, and do not follow caprice, lest it lead you astray from the path of God. Truly those who go astray from the path of God shall have a severe punishment, for having forgotten the Day of Reckoning.} (Sūrat Ṣād 38:26)

As for the social side, Sheikh al-Dedew — may God preserve him — addressed what relates to the customs of Mauritanian society, and mentioned that these customs must be weighed in the balance of the law. Among them is the occasion of marriage, in which much conduct contrary to civilised behaviour occurs, along with the extravagance and squandering of money that accompanies it.. And among them also is what people in our society reckon to be modesty, which is in reality nothing of the sort, but an unsatisfactory bedouin behaviour, contrary to civilised conduct, which the circumstances of society in a bygone age dictated.

We note here that the lecture was organised by the Future Association, which is headed by his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew — may God preserve him — and that it is the second lecture on this subject, and that it was attended by a great gathering of those who love the Sheikh and of those concerned with the work of calling people to Islam, men and women alike.

flags.arabic: عن "السلوك الحضاري" [في العنوان] مقابل "السلوك الحضري" [في المتن]
flags.context: the title of the record against the title of the lecture as given in the body, and against record 671
options: translate each exactly as it stands and flag the divergence
read the body's 'الحضري' as an error for 'الحضاري' and harmonise
read the title's 'الحضاري' as an error for 'الحضري'
flags.note: IMPORTANT and unresolved. The record's title gives the lecture as 'السلوك الحضاري' (civilised conduct), which is also how record 671 titles part one of the same series. The body of THIS record, however, gives it as 'السلوك الحضري' (urban conduct) and repeats that form twice more. These are different words with different senses, and the difference changes what the lecture is about: conduct befitting a civilisation, or conduct befitting town life as against nomadic life. The social half of the summary, which contrasts acceptable behaviour with 'bedouin behaviour', would support either reading. The English renders each occurrence as the Arabic has it, so the divergence stays visible rather than being smoothed away, and the title follows record 671 for series consistency. The Sheikh's office should settle which word he used.

flags.arabic: ما حصل في الأمة الإسلامية من توارث للحكم لم يكن سلوكا حضاريا مقبولا ... الديمقراطية إذا طبقت على الوجه الصحيح كانت وسيلة من وسائل تطبيق الشورى
flags.context: the political points of the summarised lecture
options: translate in full and exactly, keeping the conditional form of the point on democracy, and refer the publication decision upward
publish with a dated editorial note
flags.note: Editorially sensitive under style guide section 12, and tied to its date: Nouakchott, 27 February 2011, during the Arab uprisings. The summary has him reject hereditary rule in Muslim history as not acceptable and not prophetic guidance, praise then qualify the Ottoman caliphate, and treat democracy — conditionally, 'if applied in the correct manner' — as a means of applying consultation leading to peaceful transfer of power. Each of these is quotable against him in some quarter. The conditional is preserved exactly; the English must not report him as endorsing or as condemning democracy, because the summary does neither. Everything is second-hand.

flags.arabic: ما يحسبه الناس في مجتمعنا من الحياء الذي هو في الحقيقة ليس من الحياء في شيء، وهو سلوك بدوي غير مرضي
flags.context: the social half of the summarised lecture
options: translate exactly, keeping 'bedouin' and the summary's own hedging
flags.note: The same hazard as the phrase 'negative bedouinism' in record 671, and here sharper: a summary of a Mauritanian scholar speaking to a Mauritanian audience about his own society's customs, which in flat English reads as a scholar disparaging bedouin people. The criticism is of a social practice mistaken for modesty, not of a group, and the sentence itself explains it as something circumstances of a past age dictated. Translated literally and neither softened nor sharpened; the phrasing needs a decision before publication. The Sheikh's own words are not available — this is the editor's summary.

flags.arabic: وما يصاحبها من السرف والتبذير في المال..،
flags.context: the punctuation in the social half of the summary
options: preserve the double full stop and comma as served
flags.note: The source has a double full stop followed by a comma, which usually marks an omission by the summariser. Material may be missing at this point. Preserved in the English as a double full stop so the possible omission stays visible.

flags.arabic: نجمل ما تعرض له الشيخ فيما يلي
flags.context: the framing of the summarised points
options: keep the reporting frame visible and never present the points as the Sheikh's own words
present the points as direct statements by the Sheikh
flags.note: The site editor states that the points are his own summary of a spoken lecture, not a transcript. Every proposition is therefore second-hand and must not be quoted as the Sheikh's written words.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh; the reporting frame is preserved throughout. This is part two of the lecture series whose part one is record 671.

The Qur'anic rendering is interpretive and is not a substitute for the Arabic. The source gives the verse number and the sura name but not in the corpus format; the reference has been regularised, and the source's own omission of the braces has been supplied in the English as presentation.
'شورى' is glossed as consultation on first occurrence; it is not in the glossary and the gloss is provisional.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system; it is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en.
